chunk_findings.detail: The new `called_from` exception suppresses the warning/evidence whenever the command's start path resolves to the lease's recorded worktree, even if the caller explicitly identified itself as a different agent. For example, if item `TASK` is leased to `alice` with `lease.worktree=/repo/.lanes/task`, and a user runs `ddflow review TASK --agent bob` from `/repo/.lanes/task`, `ID.resolve` yields `bob`, `_in_its_own_tree` returns True, and `_name_the_item` returns `extra` before emitting the WARNING and before adding the `reviewed_for_holder` evidence. That is wrong because `--agent bob` (or `DDFLOW_AGENT=bob`) is an explicit declaration that the caller is not the lease holder; the bug's fix should avoid the false warning only for the default/derived identity case, not silence the safety warning and audit evidence for an explicitly chosen non-holder identity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/gate.py:_name_the_item

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that `_name_the_item(repo, cfg, st, "T1", "rubber_duck", "bob", ..., called_from=tree)` produces no warning and no event, where `tree` is T1’s claimed worktree and the lease holder is `alice`. That means the guard is suppressed solely because the call is made from the item’s worktree, even though the identity passed to the review is explicitly `"bob"`. If the command surface passes an explicit non-holder identity into `_name_the_item` (e.g. `ddflow review T1 --agent bob` or `DDFLOW_AGENT=bob`), bob can silence the “leased to alice” warning simply by running inside alice’s claimed worktree while still acting as bob. The stated bug is about the *default* identity being wrong in a worktree, not about allowing an explicit wrong identity to bypass the lease guard; this test encodes behavior that defeats the one-identity-per-lease protection.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_item_guard.py:test_review_from_the_items_own_tree_under_another_identity_does_not_warn

chunk_findings.detail: The new bypass uses `not agent` as the only test for “default (derived) identity”, but `me` is produced by `ID.resolve(repo, cfg, agent)`, which can resolve a declared identity from `DDFLOW_AGENT`/configuration even when the CLI `agent` argument is empty. For example, with an item leased to `lane-a` in worktree `/repo/lane-a`, run `DDFLOW_AGENT=agent-b ddflow review ITEM` from `/repo/lane-a` without `--agent`. `me` is `agent-b`, so `me != lease.holder`, but `not agent` and `_in_its_own_tree` are true, so the function returns `extra` before the warning and before adding `reviewed_for_holder` evidence. That is exactly the explicit-declaration case the comment says should still warn, and it lets a non-holder identity silently review a lease it does not hold [GR-identity].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/gate.py:_name_the_item

chunk_findings.detail: The added test does not answer the earlier `DDFLOW_AGENT` probe. It only exercises `agent=""` with an unbound `Config.load(repo)`; it never exercises an identity declared through the environment. If `DDFLOW_AGENT=agent-b` is set while running in the item’s own worktree, the CLI `agent` is still empty and `_in_its_own_tree` is true, so the guard can treat the caller as the lease holder even though `ID.resolve` returns `agent-b`, not the lease holder. That lets an explicitly declared non-holder review or heartbeat as if it were the holder.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/gate.py:_name_the_item

chunk_findings.detail: The new test is not hermetic against `DDFLOW_AGENT`. If the test process already has `DDFLOW_AGENT` set, `Config.load(repo)`/`ID.resolve` may resolve a declared identity instead of the intended derived default, so the first call with `agent=""` is no longer testing the default-identity path. The test can then fail on correct code, or pass vacuously on code that wrongly suppresses declared identities. It should clear `DDFLOW_AGENT` before building `cfg` and calling `_name_the_item`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_item_guard.py:test_review_from_the_items_own_tree_under_the_default_identity_does_not_warn

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test still does not answer the earlier `DDFLOW_AGENT` probe. It calls `monkeypatch.delenv("DDFLOW_AGENT", raising=False)` and then exercises only the cleared-environment default path with `agent=""`; it never sets `DDFLOW_AGENT` to a non-holder identity. Therefore the supported case where the caller explicitly declares a different agent through the environment while standing in the item’s own worktree remains untested: if the added `_in_its_own_tree` guard suppresses the warning based on an empty CLI `agent` plus the worktree location, then `DDFLOW_AGENT=agent-b` with no `--agent` in T1’s own worktree can still be treated as the lease holder even though the resolved identity is `agent-b`, not the holder. The test would pass because it deletes the environment variable, so the bug can remain despite the regression test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_item_guard.py:test_review_from_the_items_own_tree_under_the_default_identity_does_not_warn

chunk_findings.detail: The new suppression is keyed on the resolved identity being equal to `ID.default_agent_id(repo)`, not on whether an agent was explicitly supplied. Given an item leased to `alice` with `lease.worktree=/repo/.lanes/alice/item`, and a default derived id `default`, running review from that tree with an explicit `--agent default` (or with config/`DDFLOW_AGENT` set to that same default id) gives `me != lease.holder`, `called_from` inside the lease tree, and `who.id == ID.default_agent_id(repo)`, so the guard returns `extra` without the warning or `reviewed_for_holder` evidence. The added comment says an explicit `--agent`/`DDFLOW_AGENT`/config is a declaration the caller is not the holder and should still warn, so this input makes the change wrong: it silently suppresses the cross-agent review warning.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/gate.py:_name_the_item

chunk_findings.detail: The new `DDFLOW_AGENT` probe is set up after the config snapshot that the test says controls the default identity: the test calls `cfg = Config.load(repo)` before `monkeypatch.setenv("DDFLOW_AGENT", "agent-b")`, then passes that already-loaded `cfg` to `_name_the_item` with `agent=""`. The test comment itself states that the empty agent resolves from the config default (`cfg.agent.id`), so mutating the environment afterward cannot change the effective identity through that config path. If the default identity is bound/cached in `cfg` at load time, the third call still resolves as the derived default, takes the item-own-tree holder path, and returns `None` with no warning instead of the expected `reviewed_for_holder` event for `agent-b`; the environment-declaration regression is therefore not exercised through the claimed config-resolution path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_item_guard.py:test_review_from_the_items_own_tree_under_the_default_identity_does_not_warn

chunk_findings.detail: The test loads `cfg = Config.load(repo)` while `DDFLOW_AGENT` is absent, then later does `monkeypatch.setenv("DDFLOW_AGENT", "agent-b")` and calls `_name_the_item(..., agent="", ...)` with that same already-loaded `cfg`. The test’s own comment states that `agent=""` resolves from the config default (`cfg.agent.id`). Under that resolution path, changing the environment after the `Config` object was loaded cannot change the effective identity, so the third call would still resolve to the default identity and be suppressed by the item-own-tree case, making `ev3` `None` rather than `{"reviewed_for_holder": "agent-b reviewed alice's T1"}`. If the implementation instead reads `DDFLOW_AGENT` at call time, the test is relying on a path that contradicts the setup/comment and does not validate the config-default behavior it says it is guarding.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_from_the_items_own_tree_under_the_default_identity_does_not_warn

chunk_findings.detail: The change only suppresses the review “another agent’s item” warning when the command is run from the lease’s recorded worktree under a derived identity; it does not change the heartbeat/lease-renewal path. In the reported bug environment (a lane worktree created by a claim whose holder is an explicit identity, then `ddflow heartbeat` run there with no `--agent` and no `DDFLOW_AGENT`), heartbeat still resolves the default derived identity and does not match the lease holder, so it still reports/acts as though no lease is held. The added test covers only review no-warning, so the heartbeat half of B090201fcef remains unfixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/gate.py:_name_the_item

chunk_findings.detail: The third assertion is intended to prove that a non-holder declared through `DDFLOW_AGENT` still warns, but the test mutates the environment only after it has already loaded `cfg = Config.load(repo)` while `DDFLOW_AGENT` was absent. By the test’s own comment, `""` is resolved from the loaded config’s default identity (`cfg.agent.id`), so the stale `cfg` still represents the unbound/derived identity. Calling `R._name_the_item(..., agent="", called_from=tree)` after `monkeypatch.setenv("DDFLOW_AGENT", "agent-b")` therefore does not pass the declared non-holder identity to the function; unless `_name_the_item` is independently documented to read the environment at call time, this call is indistinguishable from the first default-identity case and will return `None` with no warning, making the expected `{"reviewed_for_holder": "agent-b reviewed alice's T1"}` assertion fail. To test the environment declaration, the test should reload the config after setting `DDFLOW_AGENT`, pass the resolved agent explicitly, or exercise the command/API layer that resolves `DDFLOW_AGENT`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_item_guard.py:test_review_from_the_items_own_tree_under_the_default_identity_does_not_warn

chunk_findings.detail: The new exception suppresses the “another agent’s item” warning whenever the caller’s identity is `derived` and the start path resolves to the lease’s worktree, without checking that the lease’s holder is that derived/default identity. For example, suppose item `X` has a live lease with holder `agent-a` (claimed explicitly) and `lease.worktree=/w/a`. An anonymous agent runs `ddflow review X` from `/w/a` with no `--agent`/`DDFLOW_AGENT`, so `ID.resolve` returns `source="derived"` and an id such as `agent-b`. The code takes the new `return extra` path, so no warning and no `reviewed_for_holder` evidence is produced, even though the review is still being recorded against `agent-a`’s item under a different identity. The original contract in the docstring is that a live lease held by another agent should warn; the fix should be limited to leases whose holder is the default derived identity (or otherwise prove the caller is the holder), not merely to any lease whose tree the caller happens to be in.
